comment: Consent capability is under-specified. Consent, authorisation and privacy are defined as foundational REDDHI capabilities, and the Lifelong Health Record has a Required dependency on consent-management services. However, the reference architecture does not provide a corresponding cross-cutting service/interface specification with the same level of clarity as the named DPI-H components. This creates a capability-to-implementation traceability gap.

public.text: Consent capability is under-specified. Consent, authorisation and privacy are defined as foundational REDDHI capabilities, and the Lifelong Health Record has a Required dependency on consent-management services. However, the reference architecture does not provide a corresponding cross-cutting service/interface specification with the same level of clarity as the named DPI-H components. This creates a capability-to-implementation traceability gap.
public.suggestedRevision: Define a technology-neutral Consent/Permissions Management service profile across DPI-H. At minimum, specify consent representation, grant/modify/revoke lifecycle, subject and delegate identity, purpose, data scope, permitted recipient, effective period, revocation propagation, enforcement responsibility and auditability. Allow this profile to be implemented through national/foundational consent infrastructure where available, or through a health-sector capability where required; do not mandate a single centralised consent component.
